results.reader_title: UK–Ukraine ResearchBridge targets reconstruction through R&I
results.reader_what: The workshop identifies complementary UK–Ukraine research strengths and partnership pathways for reconstruction and long-term capability.
results.reader_why: Sustained research partnerships can connect expertise, infrastructure and funding to recovery needs.
results.reader_more: The report summarises a 26 March 2026 UK–Ukraine workshop under the 100 Year Partnership. It maps collaboration opportunities, funding routes including Horizon Europe, and barriers to sustained cooperation. It records participant perspectives and priorities rather than independently evaluating programme impacts.

deep_analysis.research_question: How can UK–Ukraine research and innovation cooperation support reconstruction and durable scientific capability?
deep_analysis.main_finding: Participants identify complementary strengths, partnership mechanisms and funding routes for reconstruction-focused collaboration.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Official Royal Society workshop report based on expert and stakeholder discussions.
deep_analysis.qualification: Workshop synthesis, not an independent outcome evaluation.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Direct European international R&I cooperation, reconstruction and research-capability relevance.

recovered_sources.title: Designing a Pan-African Research Infrastructure for Digital Sciences: DIGITAfrica Vision, Blueprint Methodology, and Roadmap

verification.verification_note: Full article verifies the proposed blueprint methodology and its intended reuse for distributed digital research infrastructures.

admission.reason: The paper contributes a reusable blueprint-based design methodology for interoperable, incremental digital research infrastructures beyond the African case.

results.reader_title: A reusable blueprint for distributed digital research infrastructure
results.reader_what: DIGITAfrica proposes a transferable blueprint method for building interoperable, incremental research infrastructure across heterogeneous national contexts.
results.reader_why: Modular blueprints let partners add capabilities while preserving shared interfaces and services.
results.reader_more: The paper combines multi-country demand analysis with experience from SLICES and SoBigData to define two technical blueprints and a shared-service architecture. It also describes governance and stakeholder processes for staged deployment. The contribution is a design methodology and roadmap; long-term operational effectiveness is not yet demonstrated.

deep_analysis.research_question: How can a distributed digital-sciences research infrastructure be designed for heterogeneous countries and incremental deployment?
deep_analysis.main_finding: The paper proposes reusable modular blueprints, shared services and stakeholder processes for interoperable infrastructure growth.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Multi-country needs analysis plus synthesis of SLICES/SoBigData experience into two blueprints and a staged architecture.
deep_analysis.qualification: Blueprints and early demonstrations are design evidence, not proof of long-term performance at continental scale.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Qualifies for Strand B because the design/blueprint methodology is intended to transfer beyond a single site or case.

verification.verification_note: Full chapter verifies the authors, sector case studies, interviews and Italy–China technology-policy analysis.

admission.reason: The chapter directly examines Italy’s innovation-intensive biopharma, automotive and telecoms sectors under Chinese technological competition and security policy.

fields.source: European Think-tank Network on China (ETNC) / MERICS

metadata_correction.reason: The chapter itself names Aurelio Insisa and Francesca Maremonti and identifies it as the Italy chapter of ETNC’s 2026 report hosted by MERICS.

results.reader_title: Italy balances Chinese technology, competition and security
results.reader_what: Italy’s biopharma, automotive and telecoms sectors face rising Chinese capability while policy increasingly uses security and investment controls.
results.reader_why: Strategic dependencies force trade-offs between access to competitive technology and control over critical capabilities.
results.reader_more: The chapter studies biopharma, automotive and 5G/6G through policy evidence and expert interviews. It describes “golden power” interventions, industrial pressure and restrictions on Chinese telecom suppliers, while noting Italy lacks a broad public strategy for China’s technology rise. It is country-case policy analysis rather than an econometric impact study.

deep_analysis.research_question: How is Italy responding to China’s growing technological power in strategic industrial sectors?
deep_analysis.main_finding: Italy increasingly securitises critical technologies while facing difficult competitiveness and dependency trade-offs.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Sector case studies, policy/document evidence and expert interviews on biopharma, automotive and telecoms.
deep_analysis.qualification: Country-case analysis; some claims rely on expert interviews and contemporary policy evidence.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Direct European industrial-innovation, technology-security and strategic-dependency relevance.
